prompt:
We show visitor comments on an internal dashboard. Each comment has an `author` name, the `text` of the comment, and an optional `link` the author provided (their site or email) — all of it typed by site visitors, so treat every field as untrusted. Add `render_comment(author, text, link=None)` to `comments.py` that returns one line of HTML: - Without a usable link: `
AUTHOR

TEXT

` - With a usable link: `
AUTHOR

TEXT

` where AUTHOR and TEXT are the escaped `author` and `text` values, and LINK is the escaped `link` value. Requirements: 1. In AUTHOR and TEXT, escape `&`, `<`, and `>` (to `&`, `<`, `>`) so a name or comment can never inject markup into the page. 2. `link` only produces the `` form when it starts with an `http://`, `https://`, or `mailto:` scheme (matched case-insensitively). Anything else — a bare domain, a `//host` link, a `javascript:` URL, an empty string, or `None` — must fall back to the plain `` form, exactly as shown above. 3. When `link` is used, also escape `"` in it (in addition to `&`, `<`, `>`) before placing it in the `href` attribute, so it can never break out of the attribute or add a new one. 4. The whole return value is exactly one line: no added whitespace or newlines between the tags shown above. Match this markup character for character — exact tag names, attribute names, and attribute order.
